newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: First Austria seals GiroCredit 8 bln ats buy.
newsitem.headline: First Austria seals GiroCredit 8 bln ats buy.

text.p: First Austrian bank said on Wednesday it had won unanimous support from its supervisory board for the purchase of a 56.1 percent stake in GiroCredit Bank AG from Vienna city holding company AVZ.

A spokesman for Die Erste Oesterreichische Spar-Casse Bank AG (First Austrian), the nation's oldest savings bank, said the bank would pay 8.24 billion schillings for AVZ's 20.6 million GiroCredit ordinary shares, representing 51.1 percent of ordinary capital.
That works out at around 400 schillings for each share. GiroCredit ordinary shares are not listed on the Vienna stock exchange. Its preferred stock closed at 316 on Wednesday.

The deal, which requires approval by the cartel authorities, creates Austria's second biggest banking group and comes hot on the heels of market leader Bank Austria's acquisition of rival Creditanstalt from the government.
"First Austrian has created an excellent framework for the formation of a new, strong Austrian banking group," First Austrian said in a statement.
AVZ, which controls Bank Austria, agreed to sell its GiroCredit interest under the terms of an agreement that gave Bank Austria control of Creditanstalt in January.

With combined assets of around 600 billion schillings, First Austrian and GiroCredit will rank among Europe's top 70 banks and the top 150 worldwide, First Austrian said. It now held 82 percent of GiroCredit ordinary capital, it added.
"The new group will be represented in all important world financial centres and have one of the densest branch networks in Austria," First Austrian said.
"It is our aim to raise the significance and market position of the savings bank sector and make it more competitive in the future European market."
First Austria's supervisory board also unanimously approved the appointment of board member Andreas Treichl to succeed Konrad Fuchs as chief executive. Fuchs will step down at the end of June.
